panels.html:
Hilde Review

Pros

  • Considerable draw power throughout her kit.

  • AP Friendly.

  • Solid source of AoE damage.

Cons

  • Inconsistent sources of damage, split between DoT / Extra-Attacks / Multi-Hits / Larger singular attacks that can make it difficult to specialize into. 

  • Even though Hilde has solid AoE damage, there isn’t really any content that demands it currently.

Review

Introduction

Hilde is a 5-Star Void Ranger that provides backup support for their team, providing solid draw power whilst scattering the battlefield with a barrage of arrows to lower their enemies defences. Hilde never misses the mark and can still shoot to kill as well.  

Hilde’s strategy revolves around her various different “Homing Arrows” that she’s able to create from her “Quiver Reload” Skill-Card. Hilde is unable to activate these cards manually, however, whenever they’re drawn from the deck they will immediately activate due to the “Attunement” effect, when played - cause Hilde to draw a card from the deck, allowing Hilde to cycle through the deck whilst still outputting some considerable damage of their own. 

Hilde is looking to be paired with other DPS units who can leverage additive damage buffs to their advantage. Due to “Ionization” providing additional damage opposed to a multiplicative damage multiplier, units who fire many smaller attacks or multi-hit will be able to ramp up their damage with Hilde on the team. Hilde also doesn’t demand a ton of AP to function effectively either, thanks to many of her cards featuring the [Lead] tag and “Homing Arrow” self activating, this can help alleviate her AP requirements to allow you to dedicate more resources to the primary carry on the team. 

When deciding on a supportive unit for Hilde to be paired with, units who can help supplement Hilde with additional draw and additive damage buffs will help keep things moving throughout a fight. Even though Hilde has a solid amount of draw on her own, pairing her with another unit who can also draw cards will ensure you’re able to continually cycle into “Homing Arrow” to activate its “Attunement” effect to draw more cards and so on. Because “Homing Arrow” has a lower base damage value, additive damage bonuses will help with her damage output, especially when using her AoE Attack-Cards.

Hilde can slot quite comfortably into most teams when being brought into Chaos or Sortie. Hilde is quite AP friendly and won’t take away from the rest of the team's resources. Hilde has multiple different sources of AoE damage to deal with encounters that have multiple enemies, whilst still having considerable single target damage to deal with boss encounters thanks to her “Zero In” buff. 

Hilde’s main weakness comes from being split between a DPS and a Support style character. Hilde’s own damage output is split up between Extra-Attacks, DoT Damage, weaker hitting AoE attacks and stronger single-target nukes. This can make things awkward when wanting to capitalize on synergies that typically favor one of these styles, opposed to all of them all at once. 

Review

Key Mechanics

Hilde’s playstyle circulates around creating copies of “Homing Arrow”. “Homing Arrow” is an Attack-Card that cannot be directly activated, it activates whenever it’s drawn due to the additional [Attunement] effect. It fires an Extra-Attack Damage to the enemy with the lowest HP and will draw a card. “Homing Arrow” also has the [Exhaust] tag which will remove it from the deck afterwards. Hilde wants to create as many cards of these as possible to continue firing off Extra-Attacks whilst drawing additional cards to fuel her teammates' plays. 

Hilde has 3 different types of “Homing Arrow” available to her via the various epiphanies offered to her “Quiver Reload” [Upgrade] card. Each of these cards function quite similarly but each offer a different playstyle. Every variant of “Homing Arrow” has the [Exhaust] tag.

  • Homing Arrow - The default variant of “Homing Arrow”. This variant is the most vanilla option Hilde is presented with but is also the variant that can be created the most.

  • Homing Arrow (Fracture) - Homing Arrow (Fracture) is the AoE variant. Still drawing 1 card when activated, instead deals 50% Extra-Attack Damage to all enemies opposed to a single target and also inflicts 1 stack of “Fracture” to all enemies. 

    • Fracture - Fracture is a stacking debuff that stacks up to a maximum of 30 times. Fracture activates at the end of the turn - dealing 40% DoT Damage for each stack of Fracture on that enemy, when activated it will decrease “Fracture” stacks by half. This variant allows Hilde to function as a damage over time unit, whilst also offering a consistent source of Harmful Effects to be inflicted on her enemies. Note : When activated, this will deal one instance of 1200% DoT Damage to the enemy if they have 30 stacks of Fracture. Unlike Agony, where they would be inflicted with 20 different instances of damage. 

  • Homing Arrow  (Grand) - Homing Arrow (Grand) is the hardest hitting version, dealing a much higher 500% Extra-Attack to the enemy with the highest HP. Still drawing a card when played as well. This variant is the least accessible as “Quiver Reload” only creates 1 copy of this card in your Draw Pile. This offers more upfront damage but less potential draw power. 

  • Zero In (Buff) - “Zero In” is granted whenever Hilde hits an enemy when under the effects of her [Upgrade] Card “Big Game Ranger”. By default, stacks up to a maximum of 60 times and activates at the of the turn to deal 35% Extra-Attack Damage to the enemy with the highest HP per stack of “Zero In”. This is a huge portion of Hilde’s single target damage, dealing up to 1900% damage when at max stacks. 

  • Ionization (Debuff) - “Ionization” is inflicted by Hilde’s “Plasma Rain” card. “Ionization” can stack up to 12 times, lasts indefinitely and causes enemies inflicted with this debuff to take +8% additional damage taken for each stack of “Ionization”. Hilde benefits from this slightly more than her allies, dealing an additional +4% to enemies inflicted with “Ionization” for a total of +12% per stack.

The deck utilizes Quiver Reload I dupes to create a lot of her signature card. It is generally recommended to play alongside Hugo who will chain further extra attacks and gain commence on the skills played; however, it can be played for her current solo DPS playstyle as well, with the main note being to play certain buffs from Nia and Cassius earlier if possible (and looping the Attunement: Ionization with Nia's Adagio).
Synergies

Hilde Synergies

Hugo
  • Hilde plays a large amount of attacks that she generates from Skill cards, this allows her to both generate Hugo’s commence and also consume it to drive him at very high efficiency.
  • Hilde’s main upgrade (Big Game Hunter) having an epiphany that is a 0-cost Draw 2 [Initiation] has a lot of synergy in helping to solve Hugo’s main downside of having a lot of [Initiation] upgrades to play Turn-1.
Nia
  • Nia is able to increase the number of Extra Attacks that Extra Attack units can do via her Soul Riff III.
  • Nia can ‘replay’ Attunement: effects like that of Hilde’s Plasma Rain via Adagio.
Cassius
  • Cassius is able to buff multihitters an extremely high amount via his high Morale generation.
  • Cassius can generate skill cards, which can help keep max Commence stacks when played with Hugo. Cassius can also generate Attack cards, for consuming Commence stacks if enough skill cards are already being made.

Main Stats

Hilde Stats

Ideal

CRIT Rate > CRIT DMG

Desire

ATK% >= Instinct DMG%

Imagination

ATK%

Substats

Extra DMG% > CRIT Rate% > CRIT DMG% > ATK > ATK%

Maxing out Hilde's potential 7 is the main stat breakpoint to watch out for. Fortunately, it's incredibly easy to do so, and all you need is 6% Extra DMG, which can be achieved from one memory fragment's substats alone.
Investment

Hilde Potential Priority

CRIT RATE% = CRIT DMG% >= Unique Card DMG% > Common Card DMG% = Basic Card DMG%

  • 3-1: Hilde’s 3-1 Potential increases the damage dealt by Multishot by an additional +20%. Primarily useful for some extra-damage when early in Chaos or Sortie prior to Multishot being removed. 

  • 5-1: Hilde’s 5-1 Potential grants an additional +5% Damage to Multishot, and if Hilde’s Extra-Damage Stat is 6% or higher, adds an additional +5% to that modifier for a total of +10%. Again, primarily useful for Sortie and Chaos. 

  • 7: Hilde’s 7 Potential grants +7% Instinct Attribute Damage, increasing by an additional +8% if her Extra-Damage stat is 6% or higher. Quite a solid damage increase that should be prioritized.

Seasonal

Hilde Seasonal Powers

Introduces Desire Cards. Desire Cards are cards that primarily exist to give a strong passive buff from meeting certain Desire Thresholds (3/5/7) which can only be done by having multiple ally decks also made in Season-4. 

  • For Desire Threshold, it’s common to run 1 Claim / 1 Survival / 1 Inquiry for use in a variety of builds; however, it's also common to just do 3 ‘X’ to meet effect easier or do 2 'X' / 1 Inquiry (to keep Sample Collection as Card Effect). This is extremely dependent on ally desire cards and individual team building goal.

’X’ refers to a ‘Placeholder for Specific Desire Threshold Goal’, i.e. if you are building your team for 7 Claim then you might do 2 Claim / 1 Inquiry.

Introduces Persona Cards and Engravings. Persona Cards are powerful cards that introduce new playstyles or ways of buffing/debuffing. Engravings are effects that can be applied to both the Persona Cards and Equipment, functioning near identically to Refinements of Season-2 but with new effects.

  • The most common Card Engraving to take for Attack Persona Cards is [For each Lux Engraving, 1 Mark to random enemies ] or [Attunement: Decrease Cost by 1 until used].

    • For Skill Persona Cards [When this card is Discarded, activate this card] is the recommended choice, provided you are playing this unit with a way to facilitate its discard. 

  • The most common Equipment Engraving to optimize for is [When 5 or more cards have been created through abilities by allies, +30% Damage Amount to Extra Attacks of this unit (1 time per turn)]. This effect stacks. But, other damage increase effects are viable just significantly worse for Extra Attack units than the dedicated Engraving.

Introduces Refinements, effects on Equipment that allow one to get additional Equipment effects for no Faint-Cost (post-S2), and God’s Hammer, a powerful effect that gives a random copy of any other Equipment effect on-top of current Equipment but costs 10 Faint Memory and is only gained from the Boss.

  • Increase Damage Amount of Attack Cards by 20%.

  • +30% Damage Amount of 1-cost or lower Attack Cards.

  • Increase Damage Amount of Extra Attacks by 25%.

Because God’s Hammer is completely RNG at the end of the run, we do not have a specific recommendation since the player has very little control over the decision but for ATK-based Attackers usually ATK% gear is considered best and DEF-based Attackers DEF% gear is considered best.

Introduces Forbidden Cards, powerful cards that create new synergies and can only be acquired once per run (can be duped at one event or via save data editing). 

  • Forbidden: Gesture of Freedom. Permanent Cost-Reduction to  one card, can be manipulated.

  • Forbidden: Portrait of Fury. ++Draw, +Damage

  • Forbidden: Ecstasy of Violence. +Damage

  • Forbidden: Eternal Hunger. +Draw, ++AP (Ally Reliant)

Quiver Reload I: Now creates 4 Homing Arrow and draws 1 immediately. An upgrade from base epiphany that improves both consistency and damage, it’s an epiphany that can work in many different teams and builds without even needing divines.

Quiver Reload II: Gains an additional Fracture effect which applies 1 Fracture on Homing Arrow. This is ideal when optimizing Fracture damage, for most teams, as it offers one of the highest Fracture outputs Hilde can get.

Quiver Reload III: Homing Arrow ratio changes to be much higher but only 1 is made per Quiver. This version of Homing Arrow has a lot of potential with certain multiplicative buffs.

Quiver Reload IV: Becomes a [Unique] Upgrade which can create up to 10 Homing Arrow a turn but requires you to defeat multiple enemies to do so, making 2 Homing Arrow per defeat. This is an extremely situational epiphany but extremely strong and efficient in situations where its situation shines (respawning enemies/adds).

Quiver Reload V: Is now a [Unique] upgrade which makes it create 3 Homing Arrow start of turnIn many builds, there’s not a lot of downsides to having 1 of these alongside non-Unique versions of Quiver, but there’s also not a lot of upsides.

Plasma Rain II: Becomes a skill, gains draw 1, ionization buff//debuff increases, and loses the damage effect. As the damage effect is pretty minor anyway, improving the buff and effectively getting one of the most important divines for free is a rather substantial increase in the efficacy of this card that makes this an option always worth considering.

Plasma Rain III: Now applies 3 Fracture to all enemies if this card triggers defeat. This is an incredibly niche effect that requires very specific timing.

Plasma Rain IV: Now a 3-cost with [Ignition] that does piercing damage and applies more ionization. The increase in ionization isn’t much and piercing tends to be a relatively useless upgrade to cards, making this not an especially desirable option even if its 0-cost from [Ignition].

Plasma Rain V: Loses the ionization buff and becomes 2-cost but gains an innate ‘Draw 1 Attack Card of this Unit’ and Streak: Decrease cost by 1 effect. Both of the effects are a ton of QoL, with the main factor holding it back is Hilde having a high consistency that doesn’t need to make a ton of sacrifices for QoL in consistent setups, as she already likely is.

Draw & Release I: Now increases the damage buff to the drawn cards slightly. This isn’t a large increase and damage and will typically be outvalued simply from a Mark neutral, making it a lower recommendation that is situational to builds that use Neutral multi-hits on Hilde which might prefer this over a neutral epiphany.

Draw & Release II: Now applies 1 Fracture for next 3 Extra Attacks. This can greatly increase Fracture generation in a Fracture based build, but is otherwise can feel unremarkable.

Draw & Release III: Now moves all cards from hand to draw and redraws based on move. This has incredibly high synergy with Attunement: effects but is currently held back by the lack of meaningful Attunement:’s for it to properly abuse and the lack of guarantee to immediately redraw the proper cards that can make its ‘chain’ inconsistent.

Draw & Release IV: Now draws 2 [Lead] cards instead of Attack cards. In [Lead] heavy decks or when used in a more supportive role, this can be greatly preferred but is more niche than the generic options that fit her more popular carry playstyle.

Draw & Release V: Is now a 2-cost which increases next Attack Card a large multiplicative amount. The major issue with this card is the main benefactors of this buff in Hilde are not classified as Attack Card (Fracture & Zero In) which makes this buff rather underwhelming.

Neutral: Target Neutral: Mark 1. Mark 1 can allow Hilde to do a decent amount of additional damage from the card itself compared to other Draw and Release options, but there might be more specialized epiphanies preferred in the build than a simple generic Mark that it’s important to consider ‘3-star’ options that are situational but can be preferred over it. Still, the additional hit from Mark will typically be a larger damage increase than the small buff increase of Draw & Release I, making it one of the highest recommendations.
